newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Shareholders approve Westfield U.S. plans.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders approve Westfield U.S. plans.

text.p: Shareholders in Westfield Holdings Ltd and Westfield America Trust on Thursday approved resolutions at extraordinary general meetings for the group's expansion in the U.S.
Under the proposals, Westfield Holdings' U.S. arm will list on the New York Stock Exchange in May and raise US$400 million in an initial public offering.
The resulting unit, to be known as Westfield America Inc, would be the fourth largest listed regional shopping mall owner in the U.S.
Westfield America Trust plans to list its U.S. vehicle CenterMark Properties Inc as Westfield America Inc, diluting its 67.2 percent stake to about 50 percent.
Westfield America would then buy Westfield Holding's 50 percent stake in the Garden State Plaza shopping centre in New Jersey for US$145 million.
About US$15 million would be used to purchase options over 9.8 million shares in Westfield Holdings, and the remaing US$240 million would be used for acquisitions and working capital.

Westfield chairman Frank Lowy told shareholders the U.S. listing and capital raising would ensure greater access to capital markets, expand Westfield America's capital and asset base, and enable the company to be more competitive in future acquisitions.
Asked about potential acquisitions, Lowy told the meeting the group was contemplating certain prospects and would make a purchase as soon as possible.
The offering was planned for May, but could be delayed if U.S. market conditions were unsatisfactory.
"If the market is stable and the price is right, we will go ahead. If it isn't we will delay it," he later told Reuters.
"There is no particular pressure for us to do it right now, but we would like to do it."
Westfield shares were steady at A$21.20 at 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT). Westfield America Trust units were up one cent at A$1.10.
